title: AMC Sunday Ecstatic Dance w/ Ted Riskin
description:
Asheville Movement Collective
Sunday, May 17th
1st Dance Wave 8:30\-10:30am \| Warmup 8:30am \| Opening Circle 9am
2nd Dance Wave 10:30\-12:30am \| Warmup 10:30am \| Opening Circle 11am
DJ \| Facilitator Ted Riskin

Intention: Let go of the banana!

You may have heard the parable of a simple way to catch monkeys in the jungle. Leave a banana in a container with an opening large enough for the monkey’s hand, but small enough that it can’t remove its hand while grasping the banana. Even as a hunter approaches, the monkey won’t release the banana so it can escape.

What is the banana that is keeping you stuck because you won’t let it go? Approval or acceptance of your lifestyle choices from a parent? Permission to set a boundary? Needing to prove your point or win the argument?
You are invited to release some bananas in Sunday’s dance and grieve their loss.

About the Facilitator \| DJ
Ted Riskin is interested in anything that can get him out of his head, and music and movement do a pretty good job of that. He hopes to offer music that facilitates an inner journey and invitations that create a shift. While he likes modern electronic music, he can’t create a mix without including lots of natural instruments and voices. Due to a short attention span, he mixes in lots of different musical genres. title: Flourish: A Transformational Day Retreat in the Blue Ridge Mountains
description:
Awakening Asheville
**A paid, full-day retreat held in a beautiful temple on the stunning mountain grounds of Compassionate Expressions in Leicester, North Carolina. [LEARN MORE & REGISTER HERE.](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/flourish-a-transformational-day-retreat-in-the-blue-ridge-mountains-registration-1984650601374?aff=ebdsoporgprofile)**

***\*Earlybird Discount: Use code "FLOURISH" before April 4th to receive $30 off your ticket***

Surrounded by open skies and sweeping mountain views, this day retreat is an invitation to step out of the busy pace of life and into something more spacious through the exploration of movement, breath, sound, ritual, and connection.

**The Flow of Your Experience:**

* An opening circle to arrive, ground, and set intentions for the day
* Qoya-inspired movement to awaken and reconnect with your body
* A shared nourishing midday meal with organic, local ingredients, prepared by a private chef
* Guided circular breathwork with Reiki support to release tension, restore balance, and deepen presence
* An intricate sound healing journey with crystal bowls, gongs, chimes, ocean drums, and other therapeutic instruments
* Time outdoors on the mountain grounds for a special planting intention ritual
* A closing circle to share and honor what you’re carrying forward

*Note: There will be pockets of integration space throughout the day to journal, reflect, and connect with others*

Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

## **AVL Digital Dads Get Together**

Being a dad changes everything. Working remotely changes everything, too. Many of us are figuring out both at the same time, often without much local community around it.

**AVL Digital Dads** is a casual meetup for dads in Asheville who want to connect with others in a similar season of life.
Whether you’re a new dad, a seasoned one, or somewhere in between, this is a chance to:

* Get out of the house
* Talk about work, life, and everything in between
* Or just grab a drink and hang out

For this meetup, we are encouraging dads to bring their families! Bring your kids and give your spouse a break ... or bring everyone ... or bring a friend ... whatever you want!

title: Gardens of Haywood Community College + 3 Laps of the Bobcat Trail
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Three laps on the Bobcat Trail amounts to 3.1 miles. Bobcat consists of both natural and paved surfaces. There is a little elevation change on the route, but nothing too strenuous.

We will stop to look at a different garden on each counterclockwise lap. The first lap we will stop at the Bird and Butterfly Garden. The second lap we will stop at the Dahlia Garden. The third lap we will stop at the Rhododendron Garden. All three should be in beautiful bloom. Bring your camera!

As you enter the campus from Jones Cove Road, go to the first parking lot on the left. We will gather there and then head out.

Be sure to dress for the weather. Consider sunscreen and a hat. I'm going to wear tennis shoes, unless it has rained a lot recently (in which case, I will wear light hiking boots). I plan to bring my walking sticks.

As always, you are urged to bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should not have much problem. There are no bathrooms available that afternoon, so take care of such needs before you arrive.

title: Scenic AVL #8: Beaver Lake to Reynolds Mountain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
This route goes up Reynolds Mountain and rambles along the ridge line. We do not go around Beaver Lake because of their dog rules.

**Rating:** Strenuous (climb up Reynolds is steep)
**Distance:** 6 miles
**Elevation Gain:** 1000 ft
**Surface:** Road
**Sun Exposure: 90%. There is almost no shade on this hike**
**Pace:** 3.2 mph, best effort on push up Reynolds
**Features:** Lake views, mountain views
**Bears:** Not likely
**Dogs:** On leash
**Gear:** in winter, please bring a headlamp. In summer, this hike is very hot and exposed, so bring water and/or a hat. No flip-flops.

**Parking is limited** at the triangle, but there is overflow parking available at Beaver Lake Bird Sanctuary. If you park at Beaver Lake Bird Sanctuary, CALL the hike leader at 828-290-0886 and let me know. Please walk to the Triangle to join the group. Alternatively, arrange a car pool from Ingles on Merrimon with others in the group by making a note in the comments below.

**Route:** [Reynold's Mountain Winter Route](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/reynolds-mountain-winter-version-43fa7f5?u=i&sh=ifwm3x)

**Scenic Asheville Series:** There are [9 hikes in the series](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11ewlUM9OV8I4npc1cNNsSYOnXI0QPw2isAleXdFzEbI/edit?usp=sharing); hike them all and receive an[ attractive badge](https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1goXUXfzUBqhB4_UeCxodlk4ZPeCCgqZrWK2EUJvk_vI/edit?usp=sharing) for your backpack. Check your progress **[HERE](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XUm-X1_OhxKIi8JU5rhjsW37cAl4yYx8yB_NEjjI5Lk/edit?gid=0#gid=0).**
Special bonus for badge holders: You can always come on a hike, even if you are on the wait list. See our [highlights here](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/18cFp2Uhw8XthOFXxekBpt2LGP6ww-V7kmXQExI7Y0h0/)!

**Wait List:** If someone is waiting on a particular hike for their badge, they may be moved to Going ahead of other people. If I notice you need one more hike for your badge, I may auto-add you to the hike.

**Guests:** If you bring a guest, please add them as a plus one on the app so it will add them to the count of attendees. Make sure your guest knows the distance and elevation gain, and carries appropriate gear (water, headlamp in winter). Also, if someone comes as a guest, it won't count toward a badge, because I won't have record of their name (unless you text it to me or otherwise make special effort so that I know they attended).

**RSVP and On-Time Start:**

*If you decide you cannot come, please change your RSVP
- If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers can have sufficient notice.
*There are generally 1 or 2 no-shows on my hikes, so we don't wait for people to arrive. If you are late, you'll be left behind. In some hikes, there are "if late" instructions to intercept us.
- Notes and comments are genuinely appreciated.

**Disclaimer and Release of Liability:**
This activity involves hiking on city streets that may have traffic. Participants are responsible for their safety on streets and trails. The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. If you sign up or participate in this event you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event. In addition, you acknowledge that you agree to the Meetup terms: [https://www.meetup.com/terms](https://www.meetup.com/terms)

title: Burton St Community Association Monthly Meeting

description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

title: 2 Hr Spirited Improv Community Playshop
description:
Awakening Asheville
ABOUT SPIRITED IMPROV

**Spirited Improv is a heart-centered community experience that uses improvisational play as the container for spiritual growth, personal transformation, and authentic connection.** Rather than focusing on comedy or performance, we use improv as a living practice, one that invites presence, trust, curiosity, and responsiveness in the moment.

Facilitated by Jessica Chilton, who brings over 20 years of improvisational performing arts experience and 16 years as an expressive arts therapist, weaving creativity, spirituality, and presence into a safe, transformative group experience.

WHAT IS THE COMMUNITY PLAYSHOP ALL ABOUT?

Come see what Spirited Improv is all about. No commitment required. No experience necessary. On the final day of our current multi-week series, we open our doors to newcomers, friends, and anyone whose curiosity has been quietly calling them.

This is a rare chance to step inside the experience and feel it for yourself: sacred play, authentic connection, and collective joy with a group that has been building something real together.

Whether you settle in as a witness or decide to leap into the play, you'll leave with a felt sense of what Spirited Improv truly is - and what becomes possible when a community gathers in radical acceptance and love.

WHAT PAST PARTICIPANTS ARE SAYING

“Spirited Improv is authentic, vulnerable and connective. It meets my need to deeply feel, be seen and see others. On my first night I experienced such a profound healing experience after sharing what was on my heart. It was like a sound, healing touch, full moon energy bath that opened my heart. ” \~ Kate

“Spirited Improv is a fun and little bit edgy way of interacting with the mystery of the moment. You decide how much you want to interact or observe from the audience so you never have to do anything you don't want to do. It is an opportunity to let go of control and explore the spontaneity of life and creativity in a supportive, safe environment..” \~ Kenyon

“I got to play, move my body, laugh, take joy in watching my friends come alive, give and receive big hugs, and feel the presence of the ancestors who always join me. There’s something so sacred about being present with others while we play, witness and embody what is.” \~ Sue

title: Wednesday night Bent Creek
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
Hard Times Trailhead near Lake Powhatan Rec Area
RSVP's don't open until 6PM Sunday night.
Weather: Looks like rain predicted, will know more by Tuesday or Wednesday early, and will let everyone know the details then.
I did this hike series for many years before 2022, but I did it as a high-speed hike, and I am now doing it as a moderate speed hike. This is a numbers limited event and I expect people who sign-up to show up. Late cancellations, and those that don't show up are bumping other interested hikers, and they will not be allowed on future hikes.
If all goes well, I will try to post a hike most weeks, and for days Tue or Wed, distance, and start location, like switching between Hard Times trail-head and Bent Creek River Park, may change.
The current route is about 5.5 miles.
Please folks, this is intended as a moderate paced hike, and we'd like all attendees to keep up with the hike leader(s). This hike is intended as a workout hike for people to get in condition to do weekend hikes.
Moderate paced means 22-24 min miles, or 2 ½ mph.
As such, we do not take breaks, take in views, or snap photos along the way. Please make sure you're able to keep up with the group. This hike has always served as a good chance to get exercise during the week, meet new people, and create interest for weekend enjoyment hikes. It's a great introduction to the AHG family.
No need to RSVP "No" or "not attending" unless changing from a "Yes."
Please read the full description before RSVPing, and only sign up if you are sure you can go. Thanks in advance for keeping your RSVP up-to-date and not being a last-minute cancellation or no-show. This is an ongoing issue with Meetups and often keeps people on waitlists from being able to attend our hikes.
Hard Times Trailhead near Lake Powhatan Rec Area
Follow signs off of Brevard Rd (Rt 191) to Lake Powhatan Rec Area. The road is Bent Creek Ranch Rd. to Wesley Branch Rd. Follow signs to Lake Powhatan until you come to Hard Times Trailhead on your left, 2.5 miles. It is very clearly marked. Parking is very limited at the trailhead but there’s a paved pull-off just before the Hard Times trailhead and more parking just beyond at the Ledford Branch trailhead. We will access Bent Creek forest by way of Hard Times Trail and do some combination of loop and out and back.
Arrive at the trailhead BY 6:00. Because it is a weeknight hike, we are unable to wait for latecomers, fighting daylight.
\*\*\*If you are running behind, please post a comment on this Meetup page by 5:45 pm. There is no cell service at the parking lot, so if we don't have any advance notice of you running late by 5:45, we can't get any notifications at the trailhead and we will not wait for you.
We start the hike at 6:00, rarely do we get much later than that.
• Wear closed-toed footwear appropriate for hiking. The trail will consist of dirt, rocks, roots, mud and mulch.
• Bring plenty of water.
• Bring rain gear if a chance of rain is in the forecast.
Headlamps suggested
• Dogs on leashes the whole time are welcome. This is an active mountain bike area and it can get messy with dogs running loose among hikers and mountain bikers.
Please make sure to keep your RSVP up-to-date. You don't want to be "that person" who cancels last minute or no-shows and keeps someone from joining in if there's a waitlist. Thanks for your consideration - it is appreciated!
Feel free to post questions not covered in this description in the comments section.
Thanks - we'll see you on the trail!

The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. If you sign up or participate in this event you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event. title: Third Thursday: Small Business Appreciation Night featuring Jackson Grimm and Clint Roberts of Holler Choir
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Celebrate Small Business Month at May’s Third Thursday until 9pm with a special Small Business Appreciation Night, presented by Bank of America, at the Asheville Art Museum. In conjunction with the exhibition In a New Light: American Impressionism 1870–1940, Works from the Bank of America Collection, enjoy an afternoon and evening of community connection featuring live music, hands‑on creativity, and more. 
As the evening unfolds, Asheville-based, nationally recognized musicians Jackson Grimm and Clint Roberts will perform in the Museum’s Windgate Foundation Atrium from 6–8 pm. Grimm and Roberts—also members of the popular band Holler Choir—blend old-time and swing band traditions with indie rock, creating a sound that’s both unique and deeply satisfying. 
Settle in and enjoy the music, grab a drink from the Perspective Café pop‑up bar, then stroll the galleries and experience your favorite artworks after hours. Don’t forget to stop by the Studio to silkscreen your own poster to take home—a creative keepsake from a night celebrating art, music, small businesses, and our vibrant local community. 
ABOUT THE MUSICIANS

Jackson Grimm is an accomplished and respected band leader, multi-instrumentalist and teacher in the Western North Carolina music community. His songs marry folk pop melodies with the lonesome sound of traditional Appalachian music. In a region with a strong music culture, it is no surprise that Grimm’s songwriting is representative of his musical birthplace: Asheville. 
Grimm won the 2025 LEAF Songwriting competition and has been a 2 year finalist for the Songwriter Serenade. He has shared the stage with and opened up for acts such as Molly Tuttle, Sierra Ferrell, Shadowgrass, the Wilder Flower, Arlo Guthrie, Tim Grimm, Ben Bedford, Ordinary Elephant, Nathan Evans Fox, and more.” 
Clint Roberts was raised in the Appalachian mountains of Western North Carolina and crafts songs that bridge the gap between the region’s deep-rooted folk traditions and the contemporary Americana heard on national airwaves. After dedicating a decade to his solo singer-songwriter career beginning in his early twenties, Clint founded the collective-driven string band Holler Choir in Asheville in 2021. 
Since then, Holler Choir has toured extensively across the United States and expanded its creative reach by becoming the backing band for a second project, the Susto String Band, formed in collaboration with the band Susto. In 2024, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Jackson Grimm joined both Holler Choir and the Susto String Band and now co-leads the project alongside Clint.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: May 23rd Community Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space.[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-23rd-community-cuddles)**[Click HERE to register!](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-23rd-community-cuddles)**

**This is a non-sexual touch based event that invites participants to explore platonic intimacy in a safe environment** with like-minded people. We respect personal boundaries and through a supportive framework of mutual agreements that maximize safety and create a space of easy openness and compassionate connection.
At this event we have the chance to normalize touch with clear boundaries; this is a space for respectful, consent-based touch. We allow ourselves to be seen. We have fun.
We welcome people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, relationship styles, sexualities, sizes, and ages (18+).

**THE RULES**
1\. Clothes stay on for the whole event\.
2\. You do not have to touch anyone at this event\.
3\. You must receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone\.
4\. Take care of yourself and those you choose to interact with\.
5\. Speak up if you have a question\, concern\, or if you need assistance with anything during the event\.
6\. All emotions are welcome\- we love vulnerability\.
**WHY CUDDLE?**
Touch is a basic human need, and many of us do not get enough; most people don’t even know they are missing touch, or have a way to ask for touch without sexualizing it. We believe deeply in the power of touch, and the importance of communication and consent in creating a safe space for touch.
CUDDLING WITH STRANGERS
Cuddling with strangers sounds weird or scary to most people. “Will I like it?” “What if someone wants to touch me and I don’t want to?” “What if I say yes and it’s not what I want?” “What if I really want to touch someone and they say no?” These are all normal questions. The answer is that this is a space created to ask for exactly what you want, and receive NOTHING you don’t want. Many people start out nervous at a cuddle event & most are really glad they came.

**Schedule:**
6:50-7pm: Arrive with snacks to share! Get comfortable, meet, mingle, & snack.
7:05pm: Welcome Circle- its mandatory. We will set our container, talk about personal boundaries, communication, & consent.
7:15pm: Icebreakers and connective activities.
8:00pm: Open cuddling! You MUST ask and get a verbal ‘yes’ before touching or cuddling with anybody at this event. If you are not sure how to do this – great! – we will talk about it during the welcome circle.
10:50pm: Closing Circle, cleanup and head home.
**ETIQUETTE**

* ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle. The Welcome Circle serves the purpose of creating the safe space for consensual, non-sexual touch between participants and making sure that everyone is informed about consent.
* Please arrive clean & as scent free as possible.
* BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share, a friend, a date – whatever cuddle accessories you like! The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

These events are not "gender balanced".

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy-
Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid/flu.
Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event.
No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Raphael Revealed
location: NC
description:
Marking the 500th anniversary of Raphael’s death, the greatest exhibition ever held of his works took place in Rome. Exhibition on Screen was granted exclusive access to this once-in-a-lifetime show. With over two hundred masterpieces, including paintings and drawings – over a hundred of which have been brought together for the first time – this major exhibition celebrates the life and work of Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino. 
With unprecedented loans from the Louvre, Uffizi, National Gallery of Art, the Prado Museum and more, the exhibition and this film provide an unprecedented opportunity to see the breadth of Raphael’s skill, creativity and ingenuity. Award-winning director Phil Grabsky provides a fresh look at this giant of the Renaissance, and shows why he is considered one of the all-time greats. The film covers his life in Rome, and includes unique footage of the ancient Rome that was such a powerful influence, including rare footage of Nero’s Golden House that Raphael himself visited. 
More than just a painter, Raphael was one of the most extraordinary artists of the Renaissance but is often misunderstood or mythologised. On the basis of this extraordinary exhibition in Rome, this film allows Raphael, for the first time, to be truly revealed. Directed by Phil Grabsky.

title: Holiday Weekend Sunday Walk at Little Champion Plant in Waynesville
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
What better way to spend the Sunday afternoon before Memorial Day than by walking with a meetup group?

Old Timers call this property on Old Howell Mill Road near Old Asheville Highway "Little Champion" because the Canton Champion Paper Mill put in this plant to put wax on paper for making milk cartons. The Mill changed hands several times, but the Old Timers kept calling it Little Champion. (Note that Google Maps calls it Evergreen Packaging, and the sign on the building now says Suzano.)

The 3/4-mile walking track at Little Champion runs by Richland Creek with lots of creekside trees, by fishing spots, and by a picnic area. There is a bathroom in the middle of the track. We plan to do 4 clockwise laps. (Yes, you are free to do fewer or even more!) That will make a total of 5 KM/3.1 miles.

Be sure you enter the property on the Old Asheville Highway (east) side of the plant (the side with the Suzano sign) on Ken Thompson Drive, go to the rear of the building, and then turning left, go ***all the way to the far end of the back of the parking lot, down by the sign designating the Drop Lot***. It is in that corner of the parking lot where we will assemble. (If you go down the stairs into the middle of the track, you will be in the wrong place and will miss where the group is assembling.)

Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. There is a little hill on each lap, so some may want walking sticks. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. This is a paved track, so tennis shoes will be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers will have no problem.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

title: Code with Asheville Monthly Meeting
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Are you curious or even passionate about using advocacy, technology and sensible design to create more equitable social and civic structures in Western North Carolina?

Whether you call yourself an organizer, a technologist, a designer, planner, concerned resident, all of the above or something else entirely, we want to be in relationship and build community together with you.
Check out a list of our current projects: [https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects](https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects)

What to expect:
Since project work takes place asynchronously—individually and in smaller squads—the goals of our monthly gatherings are to:

* build relationships and learn about each other's skills, interests and goals,
* learn what we are doing across the organization (project updates),
* provide opportunities to get involved with and/or initiate projects, and
* shape where we are going as an organization, co-creating the culture and course of our work together.

In this meeting, we will:

* gather virtually using Google Meet for group video chat,
* do brief introductions, with a prompt,
* share updates about the projects that we're working on, highlighting deliverables for the next month and areas where additional resources would be useful, and
* discuss proposals and new opportunities to engage with local government and community organizations.

It isn't all glamorous, but the stakes are low for showing up and we'd be delighted to join together with you in this work.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: May 29th An Evening of Spicy/Sensual Snuggles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space.[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-29th-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)**[CLICK HERE TO PURCHASE YOU TICKET AND RESERVE YOUR SPACE FOR THIS EVENT.](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-29th-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-29th-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)

**What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?**
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.
-People who are homophobic, racist, sexist, ageist, ableist…
-People under 18 years of age.
***Schedule of the Evening***

* 6:50pm Doors Open, Mix & Mingle
* 7:00pm We gather in a circle to meet each other, build a container, cover consent and boundary setting and discuss event agreements. Then we will play a few intimacy building games to meet and connect with other people in the room. Please make sure you arrive on-time!
* 8:15pm Once the container is built we will have self directed snuggling and sensual interactions until the end of the party.
* 10:50pm Closing Circle; a time to re-center and connect as a group to verbally share anything that came up at the event or to voice gratitude to someone(s) you enjoyed interacting with.
* 11:00pm cleanup & head home; you are welcome to help.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision. ](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

**Simple definitions/clarifications-** Platonic- marked by the absence of romance or sex.
Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.
Sensual- gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.
We might feel sensual when we feel someone's breath on our neck or experience a extra long and slow caress.
Sexual- having or involving sex.
Often involving one more more peoples genitals; perhaps seeking orgasm.

title: Adult Studio: Landscape // Wild and Free
location: NC
description:
Join instructor Ehren Fritz Gerhard in this three-hour session of plein air painting on location at Zealandia Estate! Students will interpret the landscape using a combination of abstract and realistic painting techniques. Learn how to utilize a limited color palette and limited brushes to emphasize the fundamental structure of your paintings. Minimalism in the landscape, expressive color palettes, bold brushstrokes, and visual contrast will be the primary focus of this session accompanied by instructor demonstration, guidance, and group critique. 
Ehren Fritz Gerhard completed his Master of Fine Arts from Arizona State University in 2013 and Bachelor of Arts from Florida Gulf Coast University in 2009.  He has been an Adjunct Professor of Drawing and Printmaking at Florida Gulf Coast University as well as Basic Design and Color Theory at Florida Southwestern State College. He lives in Asheville, North Carolina with his wife, daughter, son, and dog where he maintains an active studio, works on his garden and goes on primitive camping and fishing trips as often as possible.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Bonsai Update: Walking the Forest Meadow at the NC Arboretum
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
**Bonsai Update: The Bonsai in the Blue Ridge ticketed event will be going on June 4 – 7. You very well may want to stay after the walk for lunch and the Bonsai event. Plan accordingly.**

Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center at 09:30 a.m. Restrooms are available at the start point.

We will walk through the Formal Gardens and the Bonsai Exhibit. Then we will make our way to the Forest Meadow, walking around all the paths. We'll go down Running Cedar Road, across on Bent Creek Road (taking the Creekside Trails), and return on Wesley Branch Road.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Some may want walking poles. Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring plenty of water and a protein snack.

Dogs on leash are welcome, but are not allowed in buildings or the Bonsai Exhibit. Trail strollers should be ok.

The NC Arboretum does not have an admission fee, but they charge $20 per car parking fee (so pack as many people in your car as you can). We recommend for the driver to purchase the lowest level annual membership which includes free parking. (Of course, you may want a higher level membership, your choice.) We walk at the Arboretum at least six times per year.

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles! We will either be in the large room inside or out back on the patio depending on weather.

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. Feel free to share as much or as little as you want! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: The Art of Paper: Member Reception
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
As a valued Museum Member, we invite you to join us for the exclusive reception of our newest exhibition, The Art of Paper: Selections of Handmade Paper Works from the Collections of Jordan D. Schnitzer and His Family Foundation 
4–5pm | Upper-Level Members—register here 
5–7pm | All Members—register here 
About the Exhibition
The Art of Paper: Selections of Handmade Paper Works from the Collections of Jordan D. Schnitzer and His Family Foundation | Curated by Brett Littman with Susan Gosin and Cynthia Nourse Thompson, the exhibition features 66 works by leading artists of the 20th and 21st centuries, including Helen Frankenthaler, James Rosenquist, Frank Stella, Jasper Johns, Mark Bradford, Glenn Ligon and others who have redefined handmade paper as an expressive artistic medium. The thoughtful selection of works chronicles the pioneering achievements within the discipline and reveals how the field of handmade paper art was a natural advancement of and response to the historic relationship between print and paper. Drawn exclusively from the renowned collections of Jordan D. Schnitzer and His Family Foundation, the exhibition highlights the inventive intersections of papermaking, printmaking and collaborative artistic practice.  
Please note:
Exhibition Previews are reserved for current Museum Members; please only register Members included in your membership. 
Join the fun—Become a Member today!

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Frida Kahlo
location: NC
description:
Frida Kahlo is a phenomenon. She is arguably the world’s favourite female artist—beloved by young and old. Exhibition on Screen’s award-winning film—first released during covid to a restricted audience – is back by popular demand with an exciting new addition from the curators of the blockbuster transatlantic exhibition from Tate Modern and MFA Houston ‘Frida Kahlo: the Making of an Icon’. 
Who was Frida Kahlo? Everyone knows her face but who was the woman behind the bright colours, the big brows and the floral crowns? Take a journey through the life of a true icon, discover her art, and uncover the true story of her rebellious, passionate and turbulent life. 
Making use of the latest technology to deliver previously unimaginable quality, we take an in-depth look at key works throughout her career. Using letters Kahlo wrote to guide us, this definitive film reveals her deepest emotions and unlocks the secrets and symbolism contained within her art. 
Exhibition on Screen’s trademark combination of interviews with world experts and a detailed exploration of her art, with new special bonus footage from the curators of the blockbuster 2026 exhibition, delivers a treasure trove of colour and emotion. This personal and intimate film offers privileged access to her works, her home, her studio and highlights the source of her feverish creativity, her resilience and her unmatched lust for life, beauty and revolution. 
Created in close collaboration with world experts and those who knew her. Featuring additional new material from the curators of the groundbreaking new Tate Modern and MFA Houston exhibition. Directed by Ali Ray.

title: Summer Art Camp | Ancient to Modern: Mixed Media Traditions Reimagined (Rising 6th - 8th grade)
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Throughout history, artists have experimented with wax, fabric, pigment, metal, and glass to create expressive and symbolic artworks. In this camp, we’ll explore how ancient art-making techniques like batik, encaustic, and gilded mosaics can inspire new creative directions. Students will work hands-on with traditional materials and reinterpret them through a contemporary lens, experimenting with resists, mixed-media layering, transparency, and texture.  
Meet the Instructor: Kristina Shriver
Kristina Shriver is a visual art educator with over 16 years of experience, working with students of all ages. She teaches at Asheville High School and serves as an AP Studio Art Reader and mentor for other art educators. Kristina designs hands-on, material-rich art experiences that connect historical techniques to contemporary practice, emphasizing experimentation, personal storytelling, and meaningful creative exploration.

title: Summer Art Camp | Appalachian Arts & Crafts (Rising 6th - 8th grade)
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Blending creativity with cultural heritage, students will explore the artistic traditions of Appalachian culture through a series of hands-on crafts. They will begin the week creating vibrant painted barn quilts and learning basic weaving techniques with natural materials. They’ll spend the remainder of the week further developing their weaving skills to make reed baskets and needle felting a landscape.   
Meet the Instructor: Kati Robbins
Kati Robbins has over 12 years of experience as an art educator, teaching studio arts and crafts to a wide range of age groups in different learning environments. She is currently based in Asheville where she works as a high school art teacher. Her creative work focuses on mixed media and assemblage, with a strong interest in collaborative and community based projects. She is inspired by Appalachian craft traditions, natural materials and the surrounding landscape. When Kati isn’t teaching or making art, she enjoys gardening, cooking, reading and hiking in the mountains.

title: A Musical Evening with Decoda & Ringdown featuring Caroline Shaw & Danni Lee Parpan
location: NC
description:
Decoda and Ringdown take the stage at the Asheville Art Museum for a vibrant, genre-defying evening of music. This special collaboration brings together Decoda, Carnegie Hall’s only affiliate ensemble, with Ringdown for an electrifying evening of chamber music. Featuring celebrated songwriter Danni Lee Parpan and Pulitzer-Prize winning composer and North Carolina native Caroline Shaw, Ringdown bridges classical and contemporary worlds together in a way that feels both expansive and deeply personal. 
This program features celebrated works of chamber music, alongside a collaborative set with Ringdown and Decoda, blurring the lines between classical, electronic, and indie pop. Kicking off the 2026 Decoda Chamber Music Festival, this concert experience is designed for devoted chamber music listeners and curious newcomers alike. 
————— 
Ringdown’s music is like calling your first love on a rotary telephone, percussively tearing out the hammers from a 1924 vintage upright, and flinging each of them into space while you wait for every heartache you’ve ever felt to quietly return. Collaborators Caroline Shaw and Danni Lee Parpan—who between the two of them have a Pulitzer Prize, a handful of Grammys, and a “Best Drum Major Award”—describe Ringdown as an electronic cinematic pop duo based in Portland, Oregon and New York City. Others have described Ringdown as the love child of Johannes Brahms and Brandi Carlile—if they were born in the same century and if Brahms was a queer woman. You decide. 
Decoda is an artist-led chamber music collective dedicated to creating a more compassionate and connected world through music. Decoda pairs virtuosic performance with deep community engagement, bringing chamber music to concert halls, schools, shelters, hospitals, and correctional facilities. 
Each summer in the Asheville region, Decoda leads the Decoda Chamber Music Festival, a dynamic training program for young musicians who seek to develop both artistic excellence and social impact. Through side-by-side performances, mentorship, and creative collaboration, participants explore how music can build community and inspire change.

title: Thursday Run
description:
Asheville Runners
Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Startribe Summer Solstice Dance w/David Starfire at Pack Square
description:
Asheville Movement Collective
Get tickets at http://startribe.org
{This is a pre-sales only event}

Essentials:
\- Doors 6:45pm\.
\- Open to ages 18 and older
\- StarTribe is booze\, drug\, and smoke free\.
\- StarTribe Dances are rain or shine\!
\- YES\, this event WILL sell out\! Maximum attendance is 500; get your ticket NOW to secure your entry\!

Dancing on the Summer Solstice...
...with your Tribe...
...in the magical setting of Pack Square Park...
...to a LIVE set with David Starfire...
...amplified by the 24 speaker StarTribe Sound System...
...AWESOMENESS here we come.

David Starfire
Headline for the Summer Solstice Dance, David Starfire, is known as the pioneer of the Global Bass genre and composer of music for meditation and psychedelic assisted therapy. Billboard summed it up best: "David Starfire brings a unique perspective to EDM."
David's Ascend album reached #7 on the iTunes World Music chart and he had two #1 remixes on Hype Machine. He's traded remixes with CloZee, Desert Dwellers, iLL Gates, Beats Antique, and SOOHAN.
David has performed at prominent festivals such as Winter Music Conference, Coachella, Outside Lands, Envision, Burning Man, Eclipse, and Lightning in a Bottle.

DJ Osiah
An ecstatic dancer turned DJ with a deep love for crafting ecstatic dance medicine journeys that break through the limiting ideas as to what “spiritual” is supposed to look and sound like. His mixes don't play by the rules. They are deep, bass-rich, soul-expanding, multi-genre, feeling-inducing meditations bringing in a full spectrum of e-motions that synchronistically match the vibe-sense context of the present moment at hand.

The StarTribe Vision
At StarTribe, we treasure finding solace in the company of kindred spirits, sharing love, joy, and the magic of dance.
It's unanimous: StarTribe dances are where the human spirit shines bright. (We don't call ourselves StarTribe for nothin'!)
Togetherness is the spirit of StarTribe, and you are warmly invited.

title: Father's Day Walk of the Western End of Maggie Valley
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet at Maggie Methodist, 4192 Soco Rd., Maggie Valley 28751, in the corner of the parking lot closest to Soco Rd., but furthest from the church building. We will meet at 2:00 p.m. There are no restrooms at the start point, so take care of any needs before you arrive.

The walk is pretty flat. Tennis shoes are fine; walking poles aren't needed. Dress appropriately for the weather. Bring lots of water and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Strollers are fine.

We will walk west on Soco Road to Fie Top, with one or two side excursions. We will cross Soco Road and then walk east on the opposite side of Soco Road as far as Town Hall. We will cross the road and head west again, finally returning to the Start Point.

Sights along the way include Mary Rathbone Rich Park, Tube World, and Joey's Pancake House.

This is a short, easy walk, about 3 miles, mostly on pavement. Hope to see you there!

title: Code with Asheville Monthly Meeting
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Are you curious or even passionate about using advocacy, technology and sensible design to create more equitable social and civic structures in Western North Carolina?

Whether you call yourself an organizer, a technologist, a designer, planner, concerned resident, all of the above or something else entirely, we want to be in relationship and build community together with you.
Check out a list of our current projects: [https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects](https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects)

What to expect:
Since project work takes place asynchronously—individually and in smaller squads—the goals of our monthly gatherings are to:

* build relationships and learn about each other's skills, interests and goals,
* learn what we are doing across the organization (project updates),
* provide opportunities to get involved with and/or initiate projects, and
* shape where we are going as an organization, co-creating the culture and course of our work together.

In this meeting, we will:

* gather virtually using Google Meet for group video chat,
* do brief introductions, with a prompt,
* share updates about the projects that we're working on, highlighting deliverables for the next month and areas where additional resources would be useful, and
* discuss proposals and new opportunities to engage with local government and community organizations.

It isn't all glamorous, but the stakes are low for showing up and we'd be delighted to join together with you in this work.

title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

title: Thursday Run
description:
Asheville Runners
Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: The Foundation
description:
Access Consciousness® Asheville
All of life comes to me with ease, joy and glory™

The three and a half day Foundation class is designed to break the foundation of what you think your reality is, so you can create the reality that works for you.

The Foundation class is designed to empower you to change anything and everything you’d like to change in your life. You will be given a whole toolbox that will allow you to break apart the foundation of limitation that we so often function from and build a new foundation, one of limitless possibility so that you can begin to create the life you truly desire.

What do you desire? What would you like to be different? Would you like more joy? More fun? More ease? Would you like to wake up in the morning with a sense of gratitude... happy to be on the planet?

Whatever it is for you, it is possible. Thousands of people around the world have created the life they desire by using the simple and pragmatic tools of Access Consciousness® that you will be introduced to in the Foundation class.

Everything can change.
Anything is possible.
The question is, will you choose it?

title: Game Night @ Archetype West Asheville
description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
\*\*This is a collaboration with the Asheville's Bored Game Geeks\*\*

Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!
**Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!**

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers!
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**.

**Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death!
No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.***

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary.

See you at the table!

description: Location: Enka-Candler Library - 1404 Sandhill Rd. - CandlerPhone: (828) 250-4758Email: enka.library@buncombecounty.orgEvent Type: Family Fun,STEM/STEAM,Story TellingAge Group: Toddler - (ages 18 mos.-2 yrs.),Preschool - (ages 3-5),School Age - (grades K-5),Family - (children of all ages)Library: Enka-CandlerLink: https://www.buncombecounty.org/governing/depts/library/branch-locations/enka-candler.aspxMeet Gracie, a certified therapy dog whose spirit and affectionate personality are sure to win your heart. Despite having one less leg, this ten year old "tripod" Great Pyrenees mix is excited about life, always eager for a run or swim and approaches everything with a big smile. Gracie's physical difference does not stop her mission to spread love and happiness to everyone she meets. Her empathy and willingness to listen, make her the perfect friend for anyone in need of comfort or support.Join Gracie and her parent, Lisa, for an hour at the library where you can take turns reading, petting, or saying hello! No registration is required for this program, but we will ask you to sign-in so everyone gets to spend time with Gracie. Gracie is child friendly & parents must stay with children. **Our allergy free, robot dog, Puptart will still be available on Wednesdays from 4-5 PM!

title: Historic Columbia SC Morning Walk—Governor's Mansion, Finlay Park, and More!
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet at 10:00 a.m. in the lobby of the Hampton Inn, 822 Gervais Street, Columbia 29223 (enter the lobby from the Lincoln Street side). Restrooms are available at the start point.

The trail takes you past the Woodrow Wilson Boyhood Home, around the Governor's Mansion, through the newly reopened Finlay Park, and through Memorial Park.

There are some moderate hills and stair climbing, but it is almost entirely on pavement. Tennis shoes are fine; some may want walking sticks or hiking boots.

Dress for the weather. It will likely be very hot. A hat and sunscreen are highly recommended.

**Plenty of water** and a protein snack are advised as always. Wheelchairs are not recommended, although strollers ought to be ok. Dogs are welcome.

Our Meetup group offers some version of this walk every three months. It's that good! You will surely enjoy it.

Traditionally, many of us eat at Five Guys (near the start point) after the walk. There are lots of other restaurants nearby. Give yourself plenty of time to enjoy your meal after you join the group for the walk.

title: Come sing with us! Vocal workshop and rehearsal - Land Of The Sky Chorus
description:
Asheville Area A Cappella Singers
Whether you are an experienced singer, or just like to sing in your car, come join us as our guest! The Land of The Sky Chorus, located in Asheville, NC, is welcoming guests - men and women - who are interested in joining us in the world-wide community of a cappella singing.

No experience is required; we provide music, voice training and an enjoyable singing experience under expert leadership. Our repertoire of music is fun and spans many styles - most songs are easy to learn and sing. Learning materials are provided to help you get started, and you will be paired with a singing "Buddy" so you can join in right away.

We will be here to greet you as early as 6:15pm to help you get situated.

title: EmBark Orientation
description:
EmBark Orientation is your introduction to life at UNC Asheville. Meet fellow students, connect with campus resources, and get the information you need to begin your Bulldog experience with confidence! This required program for all incoming first-year and transfer students helps you get settled, ask questions, and build your community before the semester begins. 
EmBark sessions will be offered throughout the summer. Select your date and register through the AVL Bound Portal: 

June 15-16
June 18-19
June 22-23
June 26-27
July 11 (Transfer EmBark)










    
Accessibility
UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. If you have any questions about access or to request reasonable accommodations that will facilitate your full participation in this event, such as ASL interpreting, captioned videos, Braille or electronic text, please contact Heather L. Lindkvist, assistant vice chancellor for institutional integrity and access, hlindkvi@unca.edu or 828.232.5658. 
Advance notice is necessary to arrange for accessibility needs. All requests must be made ten business days prior to the event. We will attempt to implement late requests but cannot guarantee they will be met. 
Visitor Parking
All visitors must adhere to the University’s parking policy. Please visit the UNC Asheville Visitor Parking Permit Registration site to acquire a visitor permit to park on campus. 
Event Photography and Videography
Photography and videography may be captured by University Marketing staff at any public University events. Please review our multimedia statement to learn more.

title: Game Night @ Archetype West Asheville
description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
\*\*This is a collaboration with the Asheville's Bored Game Geeks\*\*

Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!
**Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!**

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers!
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**.

**Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death!
No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.***

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary.

See you at the table!

title: Biltmore Estate: Walk the Westover Green and Blue Trails
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Located at The Inn on Biltmore Estate, the Westover Green and Blue Trails provide access to some of Biltmore's beautiful woodlands. We will loop the Green Trail in a clockwise direction, pick up the Blue Trail to walk its entire length, and then go back to get the rest of the Green Trail.

I estimate this to be about 4.5 miles. The Green Trail is wide. The Blue Trail is of moderate width. These are relatively easy trails. There is a little elevation change, but nothing particularly strenuous.

When you drive to the Inn, you will turn onto its access road. Near the entrance to the Inn is the entrance to the parking area. There are two rows of parking, an upper row closer to the Inn, and a lower row a little further from the Inn. We will gather on the lower row at the far end (away from the Inn).

If you need a restroom prior to the walk, Antler Hill is very close and there are public restrooms there. No restroom facilities are available during the walk.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Tennis shoes are fine, unless it has rained a lot recently, in which case you will probably want light hiking boots. Most won't want walking sticks, though I plan to take just one. As always, bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome. Strollers designed for trail use would be ok.

There is a grounds admission fee. We walk at Biltmore several times each year, so an annual grounds pass is highly recommended.

Many regular Biltmore guests have never walked the Westover Trails. I think you will enjoy these.

Access Consciousness® Asheville
You must be present for the entire class in order to be certified as a Bars Practitioner (BP).

The first class in Access Consciousness is The Bars®. There are 32 points on your head which, when gently touched, effortlessly and easily release anything that doesn’t allow you to receive. It’s like hitting the delete button on your computer. All of the thoughts, feelings, and emotions that keep you stuck, that keep you repeating the same patterns in your life over and over again, are released.

Did you know there are 32 points on your head which, when gently touched, effortlessly and easily release anything that doesn’t allow you to receive? These points contain all the thoughts, ideas, beliefs, emotions and considerations that you have stored in any lifetime. This is an opportunity for you to let go of everything!

Thousands of people have used Access Bars™ to change many aspects of their body and their life, including sleep, health and weight, money, sex and relationships, anxiety, stress and so much more. At worst you will feel like you have just had a phenomenal massage. At best your whole life can change into something greater with total ease.

title: Body Process Class: Circuitry
description:
Access Consciousness® Asheville
## What If Your Body Has Been Waiting for This?

## **You’re Invited: Access Consciousness Body Process Class**

What if your body isn’t something to fix…
but something to listen to?

What if it has been whispering (or maybe shouting) for your attention in ways you were never taught to understand?

I’d love to invite you to a beautiful, hands-on **Access Consciousness Body Process class** — a space where you get to receive, gift, and explore a different communion with bodies.

### What Is a Body Process?

Access Consciousness Body Processes are gentle, hands-on techniques that invite the body to:
• Release stored trauma and shock
• Activate natural capacities
• Undo limitations held in tissue and cellular memory
• Restore communication between you and your body

This isn’t massage.
It isn’t energy work in the traditional sense.
It’s a conversation — with the body.
And bodies respond.

### In This Class You Will:

✨ Learn a specific Access Body Process you can use for life
✨ Both gift and receive the process (yes, you get sessions too!)
✨ Explore how judgment impacts the body
✨ Discover new tools for ease, vitality, and awareness
✨ Leave certified to practice this body process on others

No prior experience is required. Just a body. And a willingness.

### What Becomes Possible?

Many people report:
• Increased ease in chronic patterns
• Greater relaxation and presence
• Changes in long-held physical limitations
• A deeper sense of trust with their body

But more than anything — possibility.
What if your body has capacities you’ve never been shown how to access?

Spots are limited only by space - the sooner you sign up the sooner we can look for larger locations if required.

If you’ve been asking for more ease, more connection, more *aliveness* — this may be the invitation your body has been waiting for.

Would your body enjoy this?

A body process class is a way to experience a new energy. Each is uniquely different and contributes to the being. There are NO contraindications - if it pulls you in it's right for you that day.

This class will include the body process **Circuitry**!

Registration: https://www.consciousbeing.institute/event-details/body-process-class-circuitry
